per_driver_behaviour.box: XP build VM (throwaway qcow2 overlay of ~/retro-vm/xp3.qcow2, 2026-09-29; NOT a fleet box) - the reference measurement
per_driver_behaviour.driver: Windows XP SP3 (5.1.2600), Microsoft 'Cirrus Logic 5446 Compatible Graphics Adapter' 5.1.2535.0 under QEMU -vga cirrus, no EDID, no DefaultSettings.* in the registry at first. Agent 1.93.1 (auto-updated), modetest 0.2.0 run through EXECW/LAUNCH on 127.0.0.1:29898.
per_driver_behaviour.no_freq_mode_change_lands_on: MEASURED, but as REPORTED rates only (EnumDisplaySettings, GetDeviceCaps VREFRESH and GetMonitorFrequency agree). WaitForVerticalBlank returns at once under QEMU, so every vblank reading was unmeasured (vblank_mhz=0). Evidence: .claude/evidence-refresh/review-mechanism/vm/modetest.log. ChangeDisplaySettings W|H|BPP with CDS_FULLSCREEN and no rate landed on 60 Hz every time: 640x480x24 (list 60 72 75 85); 800x600x24 (list 56 60 72 75 85, so neither the lowest nor the first listed was chosen); 1024x768x24 (list 43 60 70 75 85). This held with the registry at 60, with the registry AND the desktop at 75, and at a size with no 60 in its list. At 1152x864x8 (list 70 75 only) the request FAILED with DISP_CHANGE_FAILED and the screen stayed where it was. So XP's rule for a no-rate CDS request is '60, or fail'. It is not the lowest rate, not the first listed, not the registry rate and not the current rate. ReactOS's clean-room win32k (ldevobj.c LDEVOBJ_bProbeAndCaptureDevmode) picks the listed rate closest to the REGISTRY rate, which would have given 75, so ReactOS is not a model for XP here. DirectDraw exclusive SetDisplayMode(W,H,BPP,0) behaved differently: it landed on 75 at 640x480x24, 800x600x24 and 1024x768x24, from both a 60 Hz and a 75 Hz desktop, and failed (0x80004001) at 1152x864x8. Direct3D 9 CreateDevice returned D3DERR_NOTAVAILABLE (0x8876086A); the VM has no HAL, so this only exercised the failure path.
per_driver_behaviour.same_res_keeps_current_rate: CDS: NO (MEASURED). A 640x480x24@75 pre-switch followed by a no-rate request went to 60. A 1024x768x24@85 pre-switch followed by a no-rate request went to 60. A no-rate request for the persisted 1024x768x24@75 desktop mode went to 60. DirectDraw rate 0 at the current mode is mixed: 640x480x24@60 changed to 75, but at 1280x1024x8@60 with ForceRefreshRate=85 (85 not listed there) no switch happened and it stayed at 60.
per_driver_behaviour.driver_override_available: DirectDraw ForceRefreshRate (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\DirectDraw, DWORD) was MEASURED here. Set to 85, it made DirectDraw rate 0 at 800x600x24 land on 85. CDS no-rate requests at 800x600 still gave 60, so it does not touch CDS. At 1152x864x8 DirectDraw still failed. At the current mode, where 85 is not listed, it made no change. Its effect on D3D8/9 is unmeasured.

per_driver_behaviour.driver: ATI Radeon HD 3850 AGP, Catalyst 8.970.100.0 (13.4 legacy; ati2mtag.sys + ati2dvag.dll; the share package CX156444.inf has the same DriverVer). Monitor: DELL P2312H analog LCD, EDID vmax 76. Persisted 1920x1080x32@60. GAMERES lists 1280x960, 1152x864 and other 4:3 sizes at a best of 75, and 1920x1080 at 60 only.
per_driver_behaviour.no_freq_mode_change_lands_on: CDS (knob-less OpenGL titles: GLQuake, Q2 ref_gl, WON HL): 60 at every size that lists 60 - STRONGLY INFERRED, still unmeasured on ATI. XP's own rule is now measured: 60 or fail, independent of the registry, the current rate and list order (build VM, reported rates). This agrees with ForceWare 71.89 on hardware (.124, 2026-08-25: registry 100 at the same mode gave 60; agent/tools/refreshlogic.h). Only a driver-internal substitution could change it; ATI's DALRULE_APPLYPREVIOUSREFRESHRATE is the one candidate, and it is unset. Native 1920x1080 is 60-only, so nothing is lost there. At 1280x960 and 1152x864 (75 listed) a CDS title gets 60. DirectDraw/D3D7 rate 0: UNMEASURED on ATI, but in the VM DirectDraw chose 75 wherever 75 was listed, so DDraw titles at the 4:3 sizes may already get 75 here. That must be measured before building anything for them (modetest step 2, test C). D3D9 RATE_DEFAULT: unmeasured.
per_driver_behaviour.same_res_keeps_current_rate: CDS: expected NO. It was measured NO in the VM (75->60, 85->60, and a 75 persisted desktop ->60) and on ForceWare 71.89 (100->60). On ATI only DALRULE_APPLYPREVIOUSREFRESHRATE could change the answer, and it is undocumented, absent from the device key, and read at driver init. modetest step 1 (-a -b 75) measures it. At the native mode the question is moot, since only 60 is offered.
per_driver_behaviour.driver_override_available: The designer found no working ATI override, and I confirmed it: a case-insensitive ASCII and UTF-16LE re-check of ati2mtag.sys, ati2dvag.dll, ati3duag.dll and atioglxx.dll (7z-expanded from B156345 on the share) finds no '3D_Refresh_Rate_Override', 'refresh_rate_override' or 'refreshrateoverride'. So 3D_Refresh_Rate_Override_DEF=0 in the device key is vestigial. The remaining levers are all measured-limited. DALRULE_APPLYPREVIOUSREFRESHRATE is unmeasured, needs a reboot, and is a driver setting. DirectDraw ForceRefreshRate reaches DirectDraw only (VM-measured), is one rate for all modes, and never reaches CDS/OpenGL titles. Monitor MODES pinning is REFUTED as a raise mechanism: XP asks for 60 and FAILS where 60 is not listed (VM, 1152x864x8), so pinning 60 out of a size breaks every knob-less title there instead of raising its rate.

per_driver_behaviour.driver: NVIDIA GeForce 8400GS, 340.52 (6.14.13.4052, 2014-07-02; build matches /mnt/retro-share/Files/Drivers/Nvidia/340.52-desktop-winxp-32bit-english.exe). Monitor: DELL E2414H analog LCD, EDID vmax 76. Persisted 1920x1080x32@60. An inactive Intel HD adapter is also present.
per_driver_behaviour.no_freq_mode_change_lands_on: CDS: 60 at every size that lists 60 - STRONGLY INFERRED. Supporting evidence: the XP rule measured in the VM; ForceWare 71.89 measured twice on this vendor family (.124: 100->60; .143 benchmark doc: fullscreen games get 60 unless told otherwise, and refreshkeep lifted Quake II from 60.0 to 100.0 fps at 100 Hz). 340.52 itself is unmeasured. The switch name 60HzOverride in nv4_mini.sys suggests the driver can intercept exactly this default; its semantics are unknown. DirectDraw rate 0: unmeasured (the VM suggests 75 where listed). Native 1080p is 60-only. 1280x960 and 1152x864 list 75.
per_driver_behaviour.same_res_keeps_current_rate: CDS: NO on ForceWare 71.89 (measured) and on XP with the MS Cirrus driver (measured in the VM); 340.52 is unmeasured. modetest step 1 answers it.
per_driver_behaviour.driver_override_available: The registry switch names UseGDIRefreshRate, 60HzOverride, EnableRefreshRateOverrideDevices, IgnoreMonitorLimit and nvEDIDPruning appear in nv4_mini.sys (340.52, md5 4ac38874...), with unknown semantics. nv4_disp.inf deletes UseGDIRefreshRate on install ([nv_clearRegistrySwitches_delreg]). The device key holds no override values. DirectDraw ForceRefreshRate is DirectDraw-only (VM-measured). A measured workaround on this vendor: refreshkeep (.143, ForceWare 71.89).

per_driver_behaviour.driver: ATI Radeon X1600, which HWPROFILE reports as the active adapter (the X800 in the brief is a stale class key). Catalyst 8.593.100.0 (10.2 legacy, CX_95952.inf). Monitor: DELL E2313H digital LCD, EDID vmax 76 (GAMERES at 00:26 reads it again). Persisted 1920x1080x32@60. 4:3 sizes are listed at 75, 1080p at 60.
per_driver_behaviour.no_freq_mode_change_lands_on: CDS: 60 where 60 is listed (STRONGLY INFERRED; same reasoning as .123). DirectDraw rate 0: unmeasured (the VM suggests 75). Only the 4:3 fallback modes lose anything.
per_driver_behaviour.same_res_keeps_current_rate: CDS: expected NO, as for .123. The 10.2 miniport (md5 c0b86ecb...) also carries DALRULE_APPLYPREVIOUSREFRESHRATE, unset. modetest step 1 answers it.
per_driver_behaviour.driver_override_available: Same as .123: 3D_Refresh_Rate_Override_DEF=0 appears in both X1600 instance keys and no 10.2 binary reads it (designer's check; I re-checked only the 13.4 package case-insensitively). per_driver_behaviour.driver: AMD Radeon HD 5450, 15.200.1062.1004 (Catalyst 15.7.1). Monitor: HP 2511 digital LCD, EDID vmax 76. Persisted 1920x1080x32@60. GAMERES lists all 20 modes @60.
per_driver_behaviour.no_freq_mode_change_lands_on: 60. It is the only rate the driver lists at any mode. WDDM's own rule is unmeasured and does not matter here.
per_driver_behaviour.driver_override_available: None needed. No refresh mechanism is required on this box while this monitor is attached. modetest step 0 (-list) confirms the 60-only list.

per_driver_behaviour.driver: GDI/DirectDraw: Cirrus Logic 5436 (cirrusmm.drv + cirrus.vxd, 1999-04-23), DirectX 6.1. 3D: Voodoo 2 pass-through on the 3.02.02 kit (GLIDE2X 2.56, GLIDE3X 3.03). CRT with no EDID (the roster names a DELL E773c). Persisted 1024x768x8. Display\0000\DEFAULT RefreshRate="75"; DEFAULT Mode="8,640,480" is the fallback default, not the current mode.
per_driver_behaviour.no_freq_mode_change_lands_on: INFERRED 75 at every mode the Cirrus can scan at 75. The single global RefreshRate string governs every mode on Win9x (EnumDisplaySettings shows 0 Hz; DISPLAYCFG get reads refresh 0, registry_refresh 75). UNMEASURED; only timing the scanout measures it, and modetest -list and steps 1-2 do that with WaitForVerticalBlank (DX 6.1 HEL/HAL on real hardware, unlike the VM). The Voodoo 2 takes the rate the app passes to grSstWinOpen (usually GR_REFRESH_60Hz) unless one of these overrides it: SSTV2_SCREENREFRESH (only 75/85/120 are honoured; anything else means 60), or SSTV2_REFRESH_<WxH> through sst1InitConvertRefreshRate. Sources: our clone voodoo-cleanroom/build/retro3dfx-glide/glide3x/cvg/init/video.c lines 1062-1180 and parse.c line 1094 sst1InitGetenv (process env, then HKLM Software\3Dfx Interactive\Voodoo2(\Glide), then voodoo2.ini). The design cited these as glide2x/cvg paths; in this clone they are under glide3x/cvg. The retail kit's GLIDE2X/GLIDE3X carry the same strings (driver-strings/glide-refresh-strings.txt).
per_driver_behaviour.same_res_keeps_current_rate: YES by design (inferred): one global setting applies to every mode. Glide programs its own timing on each open.
per_driver_behaviour.driver_override_available: The RefreshRate string is the Win9x override, and it is already 75. For the Voodoo 2, a per-launch SSTV2_REFRESH_<WxH> environment variable wins over the registry and is not a driver change, but it needs an operator-declared ceiling because there is no EDID. Two more caveats: the staged Play *.bat launchers are cmd.exe dialect and UNVERIFIED on Win98's COMMAND.COM (CLAUDE.md), and COMMAND.COM's environment space can overflow ('Out of environment space'), so this route is doubly unproven on .243. Writing HKLM\...\Voodoo2\Glide would be a 3dfx driver setting and is never done automatically.

per_driver_behaviour.box: .124 (NSC-C543575F526), Windows XP SP3. NOT touched: it is the V5 6000 lane's box, and it was unreachable (EHOSTUNREACH on 9898) at 04:2x EDT.
per_driver_behaviour.driver: vcr-kmd 0.1.0.0 (OUR vcrmp.sys + vcrdd.dll, 2026-09-25) on the Voodoo 5 6000. The ICD is our MesaFX (0.1.64+ fxBestRefresh); Glide is our h5 glide3x, which reads Services\3dfxvs\Device0\glide because that key exists (minihwc.c getRegPath, ~line 1403 'on win2k, winxp use device0'). Monitor: HP P1120 21" CRT, EDID native 1600x1200@85, vmax 160. Persisted 1280x1024x32@85.
per_driver_behaviour.no_freq_mode_change_lands_on: CDS: 60 at every size vcr-kmd lists 60, if win32k hands the driver 60. That is expected from the VM and ForceWare data but UNMEASURED on vcr-kmd. If win32k instead hands the driver 0/1, vcrdd's pick_refresh (display/vcrdd.c line 88; comment line 87 'hz 0/1 means "default": the lowest') takes the LOWEST listed rate. That is 56 at 800x600 (DMT row) and 60 at most other sizes. The revised plan step 2 (800 600 32 -a) separates the two cases (60 vs 56), and the flight recorder's DrvEnablePDEV line shows the PICKED rate. DirectDraw rate 0: unmeasured on vcr-kmd; the VM suggests 75 where listed. D3D9 RATE_DEFAULT: NewDark's D3D9 display opened 1280x960x32@85 here (commit 89c000f). 85 is both the desktop/registry rate and the highest listed rate at 1280x960, so the D3D9 runtime's rule is not the CDS rule. Glide and GL titles: MesaFX fxBestRefresh (fxapi.c line 406) requests the highest listed rate at WxH (85). Our h5 Glide's hwcInitVideo then REPLACES it with FX_GLIDE_REFRESH when hwcGetenv finds one (minihwc.c lines 4675-4676; hwcGetenv line 9547 checks the process env, then HKCU, then HKLM regPath). The leftover AmigaMerlin value 3dfxvs\Device0\glide FX_GLIDE_REFRESH="75" (read 00:38) therefore gives 75. win_mode.c then calls SetDisplayMode(..., refresh), falling back to rate 0.
per_driver_behaviour.same_res_keeps_current_rate: UNMEASURED on vcr-kmd. vcr-kmd programs whatever it is handed (DrvEnablePDEV -> pick_mode, line 175). XP's CDS rule (VM) says the current rate is not kept. Plan steps 1-2 measure it.
per_driver_behaviour.driver_override_available: vcr-kmd has none today (Diag\EdidFilter and MonTrustEnvelope only shape the mode list). Because vcr-kmd is OUR driver, it has a unique conditional lever: if step 2 shows win32k passes 0/1, pick_refresh's '0/1 -> lowest' could become '0/1 -> best listed under the monitor range'. That would cover every knob-less title on .124 (the V5 lane's decision). For Glide there are per-launch routes: the FX_GLIDE_REFRESH environment variable (it beats the registry) or MesaFX's FX_GLIDE_REFRESH_RATE. Changing the registry value is a 3dfx driver setting, and the V5 benchmark plan pins refresh (ambench forces FX_GLIDE_REFRESH=60).

vcrkmd_notes:
Verified against voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd at e02dc77 and corrected in four places.

(1) Mode list and order. vcr_timings[] (common/vcr_modes.c) holds several rates per size, filtered per depth by vcr_mode_check (RAMDAC clock, CRTC fields, memory, and the monitor's H/V/pixel-clock range). DrvGetModes (display/vcrdd.c line 206) reports every (w,h,bpp,rate) with DM_DISPLAYFREQUENCY set. The order is standard 4:3/5:4 sizes first (vcr_modeorder.h), then table order within a rank. So 1152x864 lists 75 first, and 800x600 lists 56 first.

(2) 'win32k resolves the refresh before the driver is called' is SUPPORTED, with two pieces of evidence. First, the vintage 3dfx H5 XP driver, which is DDK-sample-derived, accepts a mode only on an EXACT frequency match unless every field is zero (retro-3dfx/3dfx Driver Code/H5/W2K/Src/Video/Displays/H5/ENABLE.C lines 1780-1817). A 0 from win32k would therefore have failed every no-rate game on it. Second, in the XP build VM the MS Cirrus driver received a no-rate request at 1152x864x8 (list 70/75) and FAILED it (DISP_CHANGE_FAILED), while it succeeded at 60 wherever 60 is listed. That is consistent with win32k handing the driver 60, not a listed entry.

The design's step 3 ('win32k matches the app's partial DEVMODE to one of those entries') is REFUTED: the VM request went to the driver for a rate its list does not hold. What stays open is whether win32k passes a literal 60 or passes 0/1 and each driver defaults to 60. On vcr-kmd those two cases give different answers, because pick_refresh maps 0/1 to the LOWEST listed rate (vcrdd.c lines 87-105): 56 at 800x600. Plan step 2 was therefore changed from '1152 864 32 -a' to '800 600 32 -a'. The 1152x864 step could not separate anything, since the VM result had already refuted first-listed and lowest there was 60 either way.

(3) The flight recorder records the PICKED rate, not the requested one. The INFO line is VcrDd(..., pd->freq, "DrvEnablePDEV mode %u") at vcrdd.c line 426. Only the fallback WARN (line 393) logs the requested dmDisplayFrequency. The ring therefore shows what vcr-kmd programmed. It answers 'what did the game get', but it does not directly show 'what did win32k ask for', except where 60 and the lowest listed rate differ. Suggestion for the V5 lane: add pdm->dmDisplayFrequency to the INFO line.

(4) Open question #7 (no rate above 85 Hz). 'The running build predates the 100/120 Hz rows' is REFUTED by the design's own evidence. GAMERES at 00:26 lists 1600x1024@85, 720x576@72, 960x720@75 and 720x480@85, and those rows exist ONLY in the vendor-decoded block, which also holds 640x480@100/120, 800x600@100/120, 1024x768@100, 1152x864@100 and 720x576@100. 720x576@100 is only about 60 kHz, so the missing rates point to a VERTICAL limit between 85 and 99 Hz being in force, not the EDID's 160. It is either vcr-kmd's range in force (a persisted Diag MonVmaxHz or the envelope) or XP's monitor-INF pruning. .124 was unreachable at 04:2x, so the read-only REGREADs that settle it were not run: HKLM SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\vcrmp\Diag (MonVmaxHz/MonHmaxKhz/...), the HWP22D3 monitor class key and its MODES subkey, and vcrctl info mon_src.

(5) Glide and ICD bypass: confirmed. MesaFX fxBestRefresh (build/retro3dfx-gl/src/mesa/drivers/glide/fxapi.c line 406) takes the highest EnumDisplaySettings rate at WxH across all depths, with no EDID cap of its own; it relies on vcr-kmd's EDID-filtered list. hwcInitVideo (glide3x/h5/minihwc/minihwc.c lines 4675-4676) replaces the rate with FX_GLIDE_REFRESH. hwcGetenv (line 9547) checks getenv first, then HKCU, then HKLM. getRegPath uses Services\3dfxvs\Device0\glide whenever Services\3dfxvs\Device0 exists (~line 1403), which is why the AmigaMerlin leftover FX_GLIDE_REFRESH=75 wins (retro-3dfx/FINDINGS.md lines 457-459; 'Trap' at line 2713: that value 'overrides the per-resolution refresh for EVERY mode'). win_mode.c lines 326-352 retry at rate 0 after a failed explicit rate. With vcr-kmd listing only in-range modes, a wrong per-launch FX_GLIDE_REFRESH falls back safely.

(6) vcr-kmd's DirectDraw vblank is sound. Dd_WaitForVerticalBlank (display/vcrdd_ddraw.c lines 153-185) implements BLOCKBEGIN (out of the blank, then into it) and BLOCKEND, each bounded at 200000 IOCTLs, so modetest's END+BEGIN timing works on .124 and cannot hang it.

candidate_mechanisms.name: (a) Per-title refresh knobs fed a per-TARGET rate from ONE function (gr_target_hz), published identically by GAMERES and FLEETRES
candidate_mechanisms.how: As designed (FR_HZW/FR_HZ43/FR_HZQ2/FR_HZQ3/FR_HZSRC and the matching %TOKEN%s), with the review's fixes. FR_HZ and %FRHZ% now come from one shared gr_fr_hz(). FLEETRES decides its enumeration retry on the rate list (rl.n < 4), exactly as gameres.c does. A value of 0 means 'no rate'. For id Tech 3 that is exact: r_displayRefresh 0 names no DM_DISPLAYFREQUENCY, so win32k applies its 60. Before phase 2 goes live, add three things. (1) A FLEETRES per-size query (e.g. FLEETRES -hzat W H -> FR_HZAT), so a Glide/GL launcher can ask for the rate at the mode the title really opens. (2) Rates noted only at the depth the titles run at. (3) A compatibility guard for the old-writer/new-writer window (see fleetres_gameres_change).
candidate_mechanisms.covers: Every engine with a knob: id Tech 3 r_displayRefresh (Q3/ioq3/JA via FR_HZW; SoF2/RTCW at their Q3MODE size via FR_HZQ3); Serious Engine gfx_iRefreshRate; Halo -vidmode w,h,hz; Steam-era CS 1.6 -freq (WON hw.dll has none); NewDark d3d_disp_refreshrate; Glide via per-launch FX_GLIDE_REFRESH (.124, V5 lane's call) or SSTV2_REFRESH_<WxH> (.243, needs a declared ceiling). Expected values: .124 85 at its 4:3 targets; the LCD boxes 75 at 1280x960/1152x864 and 60 native; .195 60; .243 75 only at its own 1024x768.
candidate_mechanisms.risks: Lowest risk: the rate is listed at that exact size, under the EDID vertical cap; with no EDID it is the desktop's own shown rate at a no-bigger size, else 0. Four residual risks. (1) The rate list merges all depths of 16 bpp and above, so a rate listed only at 16 bpp would be claimed for a 32-bpp title; id Tech 3 then falls to its 'next higher resolution' path. (2) FLEETRES's target SIZES (tgt/t43/q2/q3) are still a separate port of gr_decide, so byte identity of the NUMBER is only as good as agreement on the SIZE (the 3-mode-list threshold differs: fleetres g_nmodes > 2 vs gameres n < 4). (3) The rollout window, while one writer is old and the other new. (4) Halo's planned 'fall back to FR_HZ when FR_HZW=0' re-introduces a claim at an unmeasured size.

candidate_mechanisms.name: (c) refreshkeep watcher, hardened, fed the per-target rate AND bound to its size
candidate_mechanisms.how: For knob-less CDS titles on XP only. XP's no-rate CDS answer of 60 is now measured (build VM) as well as the earlier ForceWare 71.89 result. The launcher starts refreshkeep <rate> <W> <H> <exe> and skips it when the rate is 0. After the game's own mode set lands, refreshkeep re-applies W x H x BPP at <rate> with flags 0 - but ONLY when the current mode is exactly W x H. This is a NEW requirement from the review. refreshkeep today forces its target at WHATEVER mode the game is in whenever that rate is listed there (rk_pick_refresh). On a no-EDID tube, a persisted-desktop rate forced at a BIGGER mode is a higher line rate than the tube has ever been shown. For example, .143 persisted at 1024x768@100; a game at 1280x960@100 is ~100 kHz, and an unpruned NVIDIA list may still offer it. Keep the designer's hardening: no force on 0/1 (unknown), and stop after 3 re-applies in 60 s.
candidate_mechanisms.covers: GLQuake, Quake II ref_gl, SiN, SoF, WON Half-Life GL, Hexen II glh2, UE1 OpenGLDrv. Measured on ForceWare 71.89: Quake II went from 60 to 100 fps at 100 Hz (.143). Unmeasured on ATI 8.970/8.593, NVIDIA 340.52 and vcr-kmd.
candidate_mechanisms.risks: Adds one extra monitor re-sync after each game mode set. It must never run for DirectDraw/D3D exclusive titles: another app's mode change loses their primary surface (MS SetDisplayMode remarks), and on XP DirectDraw may already give 75 by itself (VM). It must never run for Glide titles or on Win9x. It is visible in refreshkeep.log. Until agent/tools/refreshkeep.exe is rebuilt, any deployed copy still carries the unknown-rate loop.

candidate_mechanisms.name: (f) NEW, .124 only and conditional: vcr-kmd's own default for a 0/1 'default' request
candidate_mechanisms.how: Plan step 2 (800 600 32 -a) settles which case applies. If the flight recorder shows vcr-kmd programmed 56 Hz, win32k handed it 0/1. In that case, change pick_refresh (display/vcrdd.c line 88) so that 0/1 means the best listed rate inside the monitor range, instead of the lowest. That list is already EDID-filtered by vcr_mode_check. If it shows 60, win32k passes an explicit 60 and no driver lever exists for CDS titles.
candidate_mechanisms.covers: Every knob-less title on .124 on every API that reaches DrvEnablePDEV with 0/1, with no per-title or launcher work.
candidate_mechanisms.risks: This is a driver change on the V5 lane's box: its decision, its gates (predeploy, benchmark comparability; the plan pins 60). It is useless if win32k passes 60. It is also the only lever that can override XP's default without a watcher.

candidate_mechanisms.name: (d) DirectDraw ForceRefreshRate (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\DirectDraw, DWORD) - measured in the VM
candidate_mechanisms.how: Measured in the build VM. Set to 85, it made DirectDraw rate 0 land on 85 at 800x600x24, where 85 is listed. It did NOT change a no-rate CDS request (still 60). At a size where DirectDraw rate 0 already failed (1152x864x8) it still failed. At the current mode with 85 unlisted (1280x1024x8@60) DirectDraw made no switch at all. One rate applies to every mode and every DirectDraw app; the dxdiag UI range is 40-120 (Wine's port of the feature, winehq 2008, citing MS KBs 315614/230002/217348).
candidate_mechanisms.covers: DirectDraw rate-0 titles only (D3D7-era, UE1 D3DDrv, Westwood). D3D8/9 coverage is unknown. But the VM shows DirectDraw rate 0 already picked 75 where listed, so measure the default on the LCD boxes first (plan step 2, test C) before adding any lever.
candidate_mechanisms.risks: Machine-wide HKLM state. Setting it per launch and clearing it afterwards leaves it set after a crash, affecting every later DDraw app. On the 60-only 1080p mode, the behaviour at a DIFFERENT size lacking the forced rate is unmeasured. It never reaches CDS/OpenGL titles.

candidate_mechanisms.name: (e) Request-fixing shim (opengl32/ddraw/d3d proxy DLLs that add the rate)
candidate_mechanisms.how: Unchanged from the design: a game-local proxy fills in DM_DISPLAYFREQUENCY, or replaces SetDisplayMode(..,0) and FullScreen_RefreshRateInHz 0, with gr_target_hz's rate for the requested W x H.
candidate_mechanisms.covers: Every knob-less title on every API. One mode set, with no watcher.
candidate_mechanisms.risks: Not built. It is a new binary beside 20+ exes. It collides with game-local ICDs (MesaFX retrogl/opengl32 on .124, nGlide). It is XP-only, and a bug crashes the game at start.

candidate_mechanisms.name: (b) Launcher pre-switch - REFUTED for CDS titles on XP
candidate_mechanisms.how: Unchanged in idea. Structurally it would also have to use flags 0: a CDS_FULLSCREEN mode set by FLEETRES.EXE is reverted when that process exits, because NT resets the display when the fullscreen process ends (ReactOS win32ss/user/ntuser/display.c UserDisplayNotifyShutdown/gpFullscreen; vcr_pace.h's EXITS note relies on the same behaviour).
candidate_mechanisms.covers: Nothing on XP for CDS titles.

On the single-threaded Win98 agent box that starves the agent, and a WaitForVerticalBlank that never returns would hang -list, which has no watchdog. verifier_notes:
WHAT I CHECKED, AND AGAINST WHAT.

(1) OS BEHAVIOUR.
Microsoft Learn:
- ChangeDisplaySettingsA names no rule for an omitted dmDisplayFrequency. CDS_RESET is documented as 'changed, even if the requested settings are the same as the current settings', which implies an identical request is otherwise a no-op. CDS_FULLSCREEN is 'temporary in nature'.
- DEVMODEA: 0/1 = 'the display hardware's default refresh rate'.
- IDirectDraw7::SetDisplayMode: 'Set this value to 0 to request the default refresh rate for the driver'; 'must be called by the same thread that created the application window'.
- D3DPRESENT_PARAMETERS: a fullscreen rate must be one EnumAdapterModes returns; the current page does not describe 0.
ReactOS (clean-room NT):
- win32ss/gdi/eng/ldevobj.c LDEVOBJ_bProbeAndCaptureDevmode starts a missing frequency from the REGISTRY and takes the closest listed rate.
- display.c UserDisplayNotifyShutdown restores the mode when the gpFullscreen (CDS_FULLSCREEN) process exits.
Secondary sources: Wine's ForceRefreshRate port (winehq-patches 2008-03; ossguy.com/?p=29 cites MS KBs 315614/230002/217348); empirisoft support thread ('DirectX always used 60 or 75 Hz' on some drivers). PST KB 17198 returned 403, so it is unverifiable as the designer said.

Then I MEASURED in a throwaway overlay of the XP SP3 build VM (details and quotes in per_driver_behaviour[0]; raw log .claude/evidence-refresh/review-mechanism/vm/modetest.log). The inference 'no rate lands on 60' is CONFIRMED for ChangeDisplaySettings and REFINED: it is 60, not 'the lowest', and it is not the registry or current rate, and the request FAILS where 60 is not listed. That contradicts ReactOS's rule, so ReactOS is not a model for XP here. The inference is REFUTED for DirectDraw rate 0, which gave 75. D3D9 gave 85 on .124 (NewDark, prior evidence). ForceRefreshRate affects DirectDraw only. All VM rates are REPORTED (EnumDisplaySettings, GetDeviceCaps and GetMonitorFrequency agree); scanout timing is impossible under QEMU. The VM ran the Microsoft Cirrus driver, not a fleet driver.

(2) OUR CODE. Cited in vcrkmd_notes and per_driver_behaviour: vcrdd.c, vcrdd_ddraw.c, vcr_modes.c, H5 ENABLE.C, fxapi.c, minihwc.c, win_mode.c, cvg video.c/parse.c. Corrections to the design:
